findings.title: bootstrap re-derives github.enabled from current config instead of job state (D1 / TC-011 violation)
findings.rationale: bootstrap() calls resolveGitHubIntegrationConfig(config) which reads the current project config. If the config was changed from github.enabled:false to true after a job was started, the resume path would resolve a GitHub token and inject it into git transport via createTransportAuth, violating TC-030 (zero token resolutions) and TC-031 (no extraheader injection) for that disabled job. D1 requires resume/reopen/attach/archive to use the stored job state's githubIntegration.enabled, not the current config.

remediation.invariant: resume / reopen / attach / archive must derive githubEnabled from getGitHubIntegration(state).enabled (job state), not from resolveGitHubIntegrationConfig(config) (current config).
remediation.approach: In resume.ts, call getGitHubIntegration(state).enabled to get the job's contract value and pass it as an optional override to bootstrap(). bootstrap() should accept a githubEnabledOverride parameter; when provided, use it instead of re-reading from config. This makes the job state authoritative per D1 without breaking the run (new-job) path that reads from config.

findings.title: Completion output for GitHub-disabled jobs omits final revision OID and attestation path (TC-051 unimplemented; JSON contract missing D7 additive fields)
findings.rationale: TC-051 (must) requires the human-readable completion output to show 'feature branch / 最終 revision / 証跡パスが表示せ'. The current handleResult only logs the branch name; it does not display the final commit OID (state.synthesizedCommits.at(-1)) or the attestation file path. Additionally, design D7 prescribes adding branch/revision/githubIntegration as additive fields to RunResultContract for machine consumers, but those fields are absent from the interface and buildRunResult implementation. No test covers the branch-published result path in run-result.test.ts.

remediation.invariant: For GitHub-disabled awaiting-archive jobs, handleResult must display the final commit OID and attestation path; buildRunResult must include branch/revision/githubIntegration additive fields in the JSON contract.
remediation.approach: In handleResult, after 'Branch published: ...', add logInfo for the final OID from state.synthesizedCommits?.at(-1) (skip when null) and the attestation path when the file exists. In RunResultContract, add optional branch?: string, revision?: string, githubIntegration?: { enabled: boolean } fields. In buildRunResult, populate these from state.branch, state.synthesizedCommits?.at(-1), and state.githubIntegration when result === 'branch-published'. Add unit tests for the branch-published case in run-result.test.ts.

findings.title: Redundant null check in traceGitHubIntegration
findings.rationale: The outer if condition already checks projectLocalRaw !== null (line 48), then the inner typeof check includes another projectLocalRaw !== null (line 50) that is dead code. Minor readability issue; no correctness impact.

remediation.invariant: Each variable should be null-checked at most once within the same conditional scope.
remediation.approach: Remove the redundant projectLocalRaw !== null check on the inner line (line 50). The outer guard on line 48 is sufficient.

Fixing F-1 should be accompanied by an integration test that simulates a config change between start and resume.

findings.title: E2E assertion permits awaiting-resume — TC-120 must scenario not definitively verified
findings.rationale: The assertion `expect(["awaiting-archive", "awaiting-resume"]).toContain(completeState.status)` after the resume phase accepts pipeline non-completion (awaiting-resume) as a valid outcome. The test comment says the pipeline completes to awaiting-archive (no PR created), but the assertion does not enforce this. The weak assertion exists because MINIMAL_CONFIG only defines the implementer agent and the fakeAgent writes implementer-result.md for every call regardless of step, so post-implementer steps (code-review etc.) likely fail to parse results and halt at awaiting-resume again. The test passes either way, meaning TC-120 (must) is not actually verified.

remediation.invariant: After resume, a GitHub-disabled pipeline must reach awaiting-archive (PR-free completion).
remediation.approach: Change assertion to `expect(completeState.status).toBe("awaiting-archive")`. To make the pipeline reach awaiting-archive, extend fakeAgent to produce step-appropriate result files per step name (inspect _ctx for the current step), and add all required agent definitions to MINIMAL_CONFIG.

findings.title: ARCHIVE_USAGE says plain archive requires GitHub integration, contradicting the feature
findings.rationale: The sentence 'Requires GitHub integration to be enabled (a merged or open PR is expected on the remote).' appears in the plain archive (without --with-merge) section. This says the operation requires GitHub integration, but the whole purpose of this feature is that plain archive works for both enabled and disabled GitHub integration. plain-archive.ts makes zero GitHub API calls. The sentence contradicts the next paragraph which describes the disabled path. The TC-075 test only checks for absence of old misleading phrases, not the correctness of this new sentence.

remediation.invariant: ARCHIVE_USAGE must not claim that plain archive (without --with-merge) requires GitHub integration.
remediation.approach: Change 'Requires GitHub integration to be enabled (a merged or open PR is expected on the remote).' to 'For jobs with GitHub integration enabled, a merged or open PR is expected on the remote.' Add a TC-075 assertion that ARCHIVE_USAGE does not contain the phrase 'Requires GitHub integration to be enabled' in the plain-archive section.

findings.title: validateJobState skips owner/name check for legacy states lacking githubIntegration
findings.rationale: The githubIntegration semantic validation is guarded by `if ('githubIntegration' in obj && ...)`, so when the field is absent (legacy state), the owner/name requirement is never checked. T-02 AC states 'enabled: true (and contract absent) + owner absent → validation rejected', but the current code only validates owner/name when githubIntegration is explicitly present. TC-014 covers enabled:true but not the absent-field case.

remediation.invariant: validateJobState must require non-empty owner/name when githubIntegration is absent or enabled:true.
remediation.approach: Add a separate validation block that runs when githubIntegration is absent: check that repository.owner and repository.name are non-empty strings, mirroring the enabled:true branch. Add a corresponding test case for the absent-field scenario.

findings.title: resolveGitHubHost uses unnecessary dynamic import in composeGitHubIntegrationForJob
findings.rationale: composeGitHubIntegrationForJob uses `(await import('../config/github-host.js')).resolveGitHubHost(config.github)` while resolveGitHubApiBaseUrl from the same module is already statically imported at the top of the file. There is no circular dependency or tree-shaking reason for the dynamic import; it is inconsistent and may confuse static analysis tools.

remediation.invariant: All imports from the same module should be co-located in the static import declaration.
remediation.approach: Add resolveGitHubHost to the existing static import `import { resolveGitHubApiBaseUrl } from '../config/github-host.js'` and remove the dynamic import.

observations.title: state.repository.owner accessed without optional chaining in GitHub-enabled branch
observations.rationale: In the GitHub-enabled identity check, state.repository.owner and state.repository.name are accessed directly. Since RepositoryInfo now defines these as owner?: string and name?: string (optional), TypeScript allows undefined here. In practice the validateJobState semantic rules ensure they are present for GitHub-enabled states, so no runtime error occurs, but the type access is technically unsafe without optional chaining.

observations.title: B-19 legacy callsite list includes GitHub-only CLI files as burn-down candidates
observations.rationale: src/cli/job-start-handler.ts, from-issue.ts, ps.ts etc. are listed as legacy callers of resolveGitHubToken/createGitHubClient and are not migrated to the composition seam. This is documented as a burn-down list, but the design does not specify a timeline. Leaving these ungrandfathered in perpetuity risks the list growing rather than shrinking.

findings.title: origin digestがportを捨て、別repositoryのcheckpointを同一視する
findings.rationale: https://forge.example:8443/team/repo.git のcheckpointを別repository https://forge.example:9443/team/repo.git に移送してattachすると、双方がforge.example/team/repoへ正規化される。digest照合が通過し、repository identity不一致checkpointを拒否する既存attach不変条件が破られる。

remediation.invariant: 異なるGit network endpointのcheckpoint identityは一致してはならない。
remediation.approach: userinfoとschemeは除去しつつ、明示portまたは既定portへ正規化したauthorityをcanonical identityに含める。

observations.title: attestation 生成: 1ジョブの events.jsonl を terminal commit 時に全読み取り
observations.rationale: GitHub 無効ジョブの commitFinalState で events.jsonl 全体を fs.readFile → fold() で走査する新コードを追加。コストは O(events_per_job)。ジョブ横断スキャンではなく 1 ジョブのライフサイクルにバインドされた 1 回コストであり、単調増加ターゲット（archive 件数・sidecar 件数など）には比例しない。既存の verifyCheckpoint も同ジョブの events.jsonl に fold() を呼んでおり、同等コストは既出。深いリゾームループ（100 回超の resume）では events.jsonl が MB 規模になり得るが、terminal commit の 1 回コストとして許容範囲と評価する。

findings.title: PR absence misidentified as GitHub disabled — display uses pullRequest?.url instead of githubIntegration?.enabled
findings.rationale: runner.ts line 468 checks `finalState.pullRequest?.url` to decide between the 'PR created' and 'GitHub integration disabled' display branches. A GitHub-enabled design-only job reaches awaiting-archive without a PR, so it falls into the else branch and incorrectly displays 'Pipeline completed (GitHub integration disabled)'. The gate must be `finalState.githubIntegration?.enabled === false` so the display is driven by the job-state contract, not PR presence.

remediation.invariant: The awaiting-archive display branch must be selected by job state githubIntegration.enabled, not by the presence of a pull request URL.
remediation.approach: Replace `if (finalState.pullRequest?.url)` with `if (finalState.githubIntegration?.enabled !== false)` (or equivalently `finalState.githubIntegration?.enabled === false` for the disabled branch) to correctly distinguish GitHub-disabled jobs from GitHub-enabled design-only jobs.

findings.title: normalizeOriginIdentity drops port from HTTPS URLs — different-port remotes produce identical digests
findings.rationale: Line 96 uses `url.hostname.toLowerCase()` which returns the hostname without the port. Both `https://forge.example:8443/team/repo.git` and `https://forge.example:9443/team/repo.git` produce canonical `forge.example/team/repo` and thus the same SHA-256 digest. verify-checkpoint.ts:238 compares digests and the mismatch is not detected, violating the invariant that different Git network endpoints must not be treated as the same repository identity.

remediation.invariant: Repository identity digests must differ for URLs that differ only in port number.
remediation.approach: Replace `url.hostname.toLowerCase()` with `url.host.toLowerCase()` at remote.ts:96 so the port (when non-default) is included in the canonical form and thus in the digest.

findings.title: AC-2: E2E lifecycle fixture bypasses required CLI entry points
findings.rationale: request.md AC-2 requires the GitHub-disabled fixture to run through the real CLI paths: runRunCore / runResumeCore / ReopenCommand.execute() / runArchive. The e2e test drives the pipeline via buildPipelineForJob + pipeline.run() directly (bypassing runRunCore/PipelineRunCommand), calls runPlainArchive (core, not the CLI runArchive), and uses runAttachVerification (core, not the CLI attach handler). The reopen path is tested only in a separate unit test that mocks ReopenCommand. This means CLI composition layer logic (token resolution decisions, config loading, dispatch-level GitHub gate checks, githubEnabledOverride plumbing) is not exercised through the real CLI stack.

remediation.invariant: The lifecycle e2e fixture for GitHub-disabled jobs must exercise the actual CLI entry functions (runRunCore, runResumeCore, ReopenCommand.execute(), runArchive) rather than lower-level core functions.
remediation.approach: Rewrite the e2e lifecycle test to call runRunCore (for job start), runResumeCore (for resume), ReopenCommand.execute() or runReopenCore (for reopen), and runArchive (for archive), matching the pattern established by the existing GitHub-enabled e2e tests. The fetch spy / credential assertions can remain as-is since they test observable behavior regardless of entry point.

findings.title: E2e fixture does not exercise `job reopen` via real CLI path
findings.rationale: AC2 requires the e2e fixture to demonstrate `job start` / `job resume` / `job reopen` / `job archive` through real CLI paths (CommandRunner). AC6 requires demonstrating that a GitHub-disabled job can be reopened and then further modified with a subsequent resume. The fixture lifecycle is: runRunCore → halt → runAttachVerification → runResumeCore → runArchive. `job reopen` is entirely absent from the fixture. The only reopen test for the GitHub-disabled path is `tests/unit/cli/reopen-github-disabled.test.ts`, which mocks `ReopenCommand` and does not exercise `ReopenCommand.execute()` against a real git repository with real state transitions.

remediation.invariant: AC2 requires all four operations (start, resume, reopen, archive) to be exercised through real CLI paths in the e2e fixture for the GitHub-disabled path.
remediation.approach: Add a `runReopenCore` call in the e2e fixture at an appropriate point (e.g., after finalize/awaiting-archive, before archive), followed by a second `runResumeCore` call that continues work from the reopened state, then a final archive step to complete the AC6 reopen→resume→archive scenario.

findings.title: README command reference incorrectly describes archive as requiring re-run after PR merge
findings.rationale: AC12 requires README to match the implementation. README.md line 243 says 'Push archive record; re-run after PR merge to complete teardown' — this was the old two-phase archive description. The implementation (`runPlainArchive`) performs record push → archived → cleanup in a single invocation without any GitHub API calls or post-merge re-run. The `ARCHIVE_USAGE` string in `src/cli/archive.ts` was correctly updated; README.md line 243 was not.

remediation.invariant: AC12 requires README documentation to accurately describe the archive command; the single-phase archive design must be reflected.
remediation.approach: Update README.md line 243 to remove 're-run after PR merge to complete teardown' and replace with a description that reflects the single-phase archive: e.g., 'Push archive record and complete teardown in one run'.
